subdomain: 1.1 Translate business problems into Claude-based AI solutions

en.question: A manufacturer wants Claude to identify the cause of a machine failure from service tickets. Root-cause measurements are held in offline lab records that the proposed system cannot access, and the tickets contain only symptoms. The business requires evidence-backed diagnoses, not plausible hypotheses. What is the most defensible design response?

options.text: Add independent diagnostic agents and accept a cause when their conclusions converge across the same service tickets.
options.note: Additional agents do not create missing measurements. Convergence on the same incomplete evidence cannot establish an evidence-backed root cause.

options.text: Ask Claude to generate a detailed causal explanation and use its confidence score to decide whether to release the diagnosis.
options.note: A detailed rationale or self-reported confidence is not a substitute for unavailable evidence. Confident confabulation remains possible.

options.text: Expose the required lab evidence or narrow the feature to symptom triage with an explicit diagnostic handoff.
options.note: The required outcome depends on an unavailable input. Restoring that evidence path or narrowing the authorized claim resolves the feasibility gap rather than masking it with model complexity.

options.text: Retrieve more maintenance manuals and treat the most similar documented failure as the confirmed cause for each ticket.
options.note: Manuals describe possible mechanisms, not the measurements for this incident. Similarity can support a hypothesis but cannot meet the stipulated confirmation requirement.
